=====publish.yml=====
name: "Static site: Publish (reusable)"

# The logic behind every static-site repo's release, vendored from the
# static-website pack into the repo's own .github/. workflow_call ONLY — the
# `static-site-release.yml` orchestrator owns the triggers and passes no repo
# values; everything repo-specific comes from `.github/site.config` via the
# read-site-config composite action.
#
# The pipeline, in order — and the order is the point: nothing is bumped,
# tagged or deployed until the tests that guard the site have passed.
#
#   check    is a release due? A push that touched the declared publish set,
#            or `force`, or a repo with no release yet. The baseline is the
#            LATEST RELEASE TAG, not a time window, so a day whose run failed
#            is caught by the next push instead of stranded.
#   verify   the repo's own gate (`test_command`), on the tree being released.
#   bump     the date-anchored version (bump-site-version), pushed to main.
#            Pushed with GITHUB_TOKEN, which fires no workflow — hence the
#            explicit deploy call below rather than a second push trigger.
#   release  GitHub Release `v<major>.<ymmdd>.<n>` at the bump commit, with
#            auto-generated notes.
#   deploy   the Pages deploy of that exact commit, from the explicit publish
#            set.
#
# The caller must grant `permissions: contents: write, pages: write,
# id-token: write, issues: write`.
on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      force:
        description: "Release even when no published file changed"
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false

defaults:
  run:
    shell: bash

jobs:
  check:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
    outputs:
      release: ${{ steps.diff.outputs.release }}
      test_command: ${{ steps.cfg.outputs.test_command }}
      sha: ${{ steps.head.outputs.sha }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
        with:
          # The branch tip as of now, not github.sha (the tip when the push
          # landed) — anything merged in between rides along in this release.
          ref: main
          # Full history + tags: the diff below is against the latest release tag.
          fetch-depth: 0

      # Pin that tip once, here: every later stage checks out THIS sha, so the
      # tree that is tested is the tree that is bumped, tagged and deployed.
      - id: head
        run: echo "sha=$(git rev-parse HEAD)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - id: cfg
        uses: ./.github/actions/read-site-config

      - name: Look for published-file changes since the last release
        id: diff
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          FORCE: ${{ inputs.force }}
          PUBLISH_ROOT: ${{ steps.cfg.outputs.publish_root }}
          # Intentionally word-split below into the individual publish paths.
          PUBLISH_PATHS: ${{ steps.cfg.outputs.publish_paths }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          if [ "$FORCE" = "true" ]; then
            echo "Forced — releasing the current tree." | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
            echo "release=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            exit 0
          fi
          latest="$(gh release view --json tagName -q .tagName 2>/dev/null || true)"
          if [ -z "$latest" ]; then
            echo "No published release to diff against — releasing the current tree." | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
            echo "release=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            exit 0
          fi
          # Repo-relative prefixes of the publish set (publish paths are relative
          # to publish_root; "." means they already are repo-relative).
          prefixes=""
          for p in $PUBLISH_PATHS; do
            if [ "$PUBLISH_ROOT" = "." ]; then prefixes="$prefixes $p"; else prefixes="$prefixes $PUBLISH_ROOT/$p"; fi
          done
          changed=""
          while IFS= read -r f; do
            [ -z "$f" ] && continue
            for root in $prefixes; do
              case "$f" in
                "$root"|"$root"/*) changed="${changed}${f}"$'\n'; break;;
              esac
            done
          done < <(git diff --name-only "$latest" HEAD)
          if [ -z "$changed" ]; then
            echo "No published-file changes since $latest — nothing to release." | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
            echo "release=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            { echo "Published files changed since $latest — releasing:"; printf '%s' "$changed"; } | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
            echo "release=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  # The repo's own gate, on the tree about to be released. Before the bump on
  # purpose: a failed gate must leave the version, the tag and the live site
  # exactly as they were.
  verify:
    needs: check
    if: needs.check.outputs.release == 'true' && needs.check.outputs.test_command != ''
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
        with:
          ref: ${{ needs.check.outputs.sha }}
      # No install step and no npm cache: a test_command that needs dependencies
      # says so itself (`npm ci && npm test`), which keeps the config to the five
      # keys and never assumes a lockfile a plain HTML repo doesn't have.
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v5
        with:
          node-version: 22
      - name: Run the repo's gate
        run: ${{ needs.check.outputs.test_command }}

  bump:
    needs: [check, verify]
    # `always()` so the skipped verify job (a repo that states test_command="")
    # does not skip the release with it; the explicit result test still stops a
    # real failure.
    if: always() && needs.check.outputs.release == 'true' && needs.verify.result != 'failure' && needs.verify.result != 'cancelled'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: write
    outputs:
      version: ${{ steps.bump.outputs.version }}
      sha: ${{ steps.push.outputs.sha }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
        with:
          # The exact tree `verify` passed. If main has moved since, the push
          # below fails non-fast-forward — a loud red the reporter turns into an
          # issue, and the next push releases everything at once. That is the
          # right trade: a release always ships a tested tree.
          ref: ${{ needs.check.outputs.sha }}

      - id: cfg
        uses: ./.github/actions/read-site-config

      - id: bump
        uses: ./.github/actions/bump-site-version
        with:
          version_files: ${{ steps.cfg.outputs.version_files }}

      - name: Push the bump to main
        id: push
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"
          git config user.email "41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
          git commit -am "Release v${{ steps.bump.outputs.version }} [skip ci]"
          git push origin HEAD:main
          echo "sha=$(git rev-parse HEAD)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "Bumped to v${{ steps.bump.outputs.version }}." >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

  release:
    needs: bump
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
        with:
          ref: ${{ needs.bump.outputs.sha }}
          fetch-depth: 0
      - name: Cut the GitHub Release
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          VERSION: ${{ needs.bump.outputs.version }}
          SHA: ${{ needs.bump.outputs.sha }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          gh release create "v$VERSION" --target "$SHA" --title "v$VERSION" --generate-notes
          echo "Released v$VERSION." >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

  # The site itself, from the exact commit that was released.
  deploy:
    needs: [bump, release]
    permissions:
      contents: read
      pages: write
      id-token: write
    uses: ./.github/workflows/static-site-deploy-pages.yml
    with:
      ref: ${{ needs.bump.outputs.sha }}

  # Release-on-push is unattended once the merge is done — a red run in the
  # Actions list reaches nobody. Converge any failure in this pipeline (its own
  # jobs and the called deploy alike) to a fresh tracking issue, superseding the
  # earlier open ones for this workflow so the newest failure is always the
  # single open bug to triage.
  report-failure:
    needs: [check, verify, bump, release, deploy]
    if: failure()
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      issues: write
    steps:
      - name: Open a fresh failure issue and dedup earlier ones
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          RUN_URL: ${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}
          RUN_ID: ${{ github.run_id }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          prefix="⚠️ Workflow failing: Static site: Publish"
          title="${prefix} — $(date -u +%Y-%m-%d) (run ${RUN_ID})"
          # GitHub never creates a label on demand, and listing by a missing
          # label errors — so create it idempotently first.
          gh label create workflow-failure --repo "$REPO" --color B60205 \
            --description "An unattended workflow failed and needs a human" 2>/dev/null || true
          mapfile -t olds < <(gh issue list --repo "$REPO" --label workflow-failure \
            --state open --json number,title --limit 100 \
            -q "map(select(.title | startswith(\"$prefix\"))) | .[].number")
          url="$(gh issue create --repo "$REPO" --title "$title" --label workflow-failure \
            --body "The static-site release pipeline failed: [view run](${RUN_URL}). The site was NOT redeployed. Close this once the cause is fixed.")"
          new="${url##*/}"
          for n in "${olds[@]:-}"; do
            [ -n "$n" ] || continue
            gh issue comment "$n" --repo "$REPO" --body "Duplicate of #${new} — superseded by the latest failure of this workflow."
            gh issue close "$n" --repo "$REPO" --reason "not planned" 2>/dev/null || gh issue close "$n" --repo "$REPO"
          done
=====release.yml=====
name: Release static site

# THE ORCHESTRATOR of the static-website release standard — the one entry point
# every static-site repo of ours carries, vendored from the pack into this repo's
# own .github/ (GitHub resolves a reusable workflow or composite action only from
# the repo's own .github/, never from a mount). It owns the TRIGGERS and nothing
# else: the logic lives in the local reusable workflows it calls, and every
# repo-specific value comes from this repo's `.github/site.config` (read inside
# those workflows), so this file is copy-verbatim in every site repo.
#
# Release on push: any push to main that touches the repo's declared publish set
# cuts a release — bump the date-anchored version, tag it, deploy the site. A
# push that touches nothing published is a clean no-op, so ordinary README and
# tooling commits do not churn the version or redeploy an unchanged site.
#
# The dispatch form re-runs the same pipeline by hand; `force: true` releases
# even when nothing published changed (a rebuild after a settings fix, a first
# deploy on a repo whose site predates the pipeline).
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      force:
        description: "Release even when no published file changed"
        type: boolean
        default: false

# One release at a time, and never cancel one mid-flight: a cancelled run can
# leave the version bumped with no release or deploy behind it.
concurrency:
  group: static-site-release
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  release:
    permissions:
      contents: write   # push the version bump, create the release
      pages: write      # deploy the site
      id-token: write   # the OIDC token deploy-pages exchanges
      issues: write     # the failure reporter
    uses: ./.github/workflows/static-site-publish.yml
    with:
      force: ${{ inputs.force || false }}

          while IFS= read -r f; do
            [ -z "$f" ] && continue
            for root in $prefixes; do
              case "$f" in
                "$root"|"$root"/*) changed="${changed}${f}"$'\n'; break;;
              esac
            done
          done < <(git diff --name-only "$latest" HEAD)
          if [ -z "$changed" ]; then
            echo "No published-file changes since $latest — nothing to release." | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
            echo "release=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            { echo "Published files changed since $latest — releasing:"; printf '%s' "$changed"; } | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
            echo "release=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  # The repo's own gate, on the tree about to be released. Before the bump on
  # purpose: a failed gate must leave the version, the tag and the live site
  # exactly as they were.
  verify:
    needs: check
    if: needs.check.outputs.release == 'true' && needs.check.outputs.test_command != ''
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
        with:
          ref: ${{ needs.check.outputs.sha }}
      # No install step and no npm cache: a test_command that needs dependencies
      # says so itself (`npm ci && npm test`), which keeps the config to the five
      # keys and never assumes a lockfile a plain HTML repo doesn't have.
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v5
        with:
          node-version: 22
      - name: Run the repo's gate
        run: ${{ needs.check.outputs.test_command }}

  bump:
    needs: [check, verify]
    # `always()` so the skipped verify job (a repo that states test_command="")
    # does not skip the release with it; the explicit result test still stops a
    # real failure.
    if: always() && needs.check.outputs.release == 'true' && needs.verify.result != 'failure' && needs.verify.result != 'cancelled'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: write
    outputs:
      version: ${{ steps.bump.outputs.version }}
      sha: ${{ steps.push.outputs.sha }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
        with:
          # The exact tree `verify` passed. If main has moved since, the push
          # below fails non-fast-forward — a loud red the reporter turns into an
          # issue, and the next push releases everything at once. That is the
          # right trade: a release always ships a tested tree.
          ref: ${{ needs.check.outputs.sha }}

      - id: cfg
        uses: ./.github/actions/read-site-config

      - id: bump
        uses: ./.github/actions/bump-site-version
        with:
          version_files: ${{ steps.cfg.outputs.version_files }}

      - name: Push the bump to main
        id: push
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"
          git config user.email "41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
          git commit -am "Release v${{ steps.bump.outputs.version }} [skip ci]"
          git push origin HEAD:main
          echo "sha=$(git rev-parse HEAD)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "Bumped to v${{ steps.bump.outputs.version }}." >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

  release:
    needs: bump
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
        with:
          ref: ${{ needs.bump.outputs.sha }}
          fetch-depth: 0
      - name: Cut the GitHub Release
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          VERSION: ${{ needs.bump.outputs.version }}
          SHA: ${{ needs.bump.outputs.sha }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          gh release create "v$VERSION" --target "$SHA" --title "v$VERSION" --generate-notes
          echo "Released v$VERSION." >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

  # The site itself, from the exact commit that was released.
  deploy:
    needs: [bump, release]
    permissions:
      contents: read
      pages: write
      id-token: write
    uses: ./.github/workflows/static-site-deploy-pages.yml
    with:
      ref: ${{ needs.bump.outputs.sha }}

  # Release-on-push is unattended once the merge is done — a red run in the
  # Actions list reaches nobody. Converge any failure in this pipeline (its own
  # jobs and the called deploy alike) to a fresh tracking issue, superseding the
  # earlier open ones for this workflow so the newest failure is always the
  # single open bug to triage.
  report-failure:
    needs: [check, verify, bump, release, deploy]
    if: failure()
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      issues: write
    steps:
      - name: Open a fresh failure issue and dedup earlier ones
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          RUN_URL: ${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}
          RUN_ID: ${{ github.run_id }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          prefix="⚠️ Workflow failing: Static site: Publish"
          title="${prefix} — $(date -u +%Y-%m-%d) (run ${RUN_ID})"
          # GitHub never creates a label on demand, and listing by a missing
          # label errors — so create it idempotently first.
          gh label create workflow-failure --repo "$REPO" --color B60205 \
            --description "An unattended workflow failed and needs a human" 2>/dev/null || true
          mapfile -t olds < <(gh issue list --repo "$REPO" --label workflow-failure \
            --state open --json number,title --limit 100 \
            -q "map(select(.title | startswith(\"$prefix\"))) | .[].number")
          url="$(gh issue create --repo "$REPO" --title "$title" --label workflow-failure \
            --body "The static-site release pipeline failed: [view run](${RUN_URL}). The site was NOT redeployed. Close this once the cause is fixed.")"
          new="${url##*/}"
          for n in "${olds[@]:-}"; do
            [ -n "$n" ] || continue
            gh issue comment "$n" --repo "$REPO" --body "Duplicate of #${new} — superseded by the latest failure of this workflow."
            gh issue close "$n" --repo "$REPO" --reason "not planned" 2>/dev/null || gh issue close "$n" --repo "$REPO"
          done

# every static-site repo of ours carries, vendored from the pack into this repo's
# own .github/ (GitHub resolves a reusable workflow or composite action only from
# the repo's own .github/, never from a mount). It owns the TRIGGERS and nothing

# repo-specific value comes from this repo's `.github/site.config` (read inside

# deploy on a repo whose site predates the pipeline).
on:

    inputs:

        description: "Release even when no published file changed"
        type: boolean
        default: false

# leave the version bumped with no release or deploy behind it.
concurrency:
  group: static-site-release
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:

      contents: write   # push the version bump, create the release
      pages: write      # deploy the site
      id-token: write   # the OIDC token deploy-pages exchanges
      issues: write     # the failure reporter
    uses: ./.github/workflows/static-site-publish.yml
    with:
      force: ${{ inputs.force || false }}

name: Read release config
description: >-

  REQUIRED `.github/release.config` (six explicit keys, no defaults) and exposes

    description: Dependency-install command ("" = no install)
    value: ${{ steps.cfg.outputs.setup_command }}
  test_command:

  ship_paths:
    description: Space-separated shipped roots (the daily change filter)

input.title: The version bump belongs to the change, not the release flow (chrome-extension + static-website)
input.body:
## The problem

Both release standards bump the version *for* you, inside the pipeline:

- `chrome-extension`'s daily auto-release patch-bumps the manifest + `package.json` and pushes that
  bump straight to `main` before packaging.
- `static-website`'s publish reusable computes the date-anchored `<major>.<ymmdd>.<n>` and pushes
  that bump straight to `main` before tagging and deploying.

Two costs. The version a PR lands is not the version that ships, so a reviewer cannot see what a
change will be released as; and the pipeline is writing to `main` unattended, which is the one push
that can fail non-fast-forward and strand a release. Claudinite itself does not work this way — a
change under `packs/<id>/` must move that pack's version *in the same change* (`pack-version-bumped`),
and a change to the engine must carry its release record (`engine-release-record`). Both packs
should hold the same line.

## The change

1. **A work-scope check per pack.** A change that touches the files that actually ship must raise
   the version in the same change:
   - `cer/version-bumped` — the change touches something under `ship_paths`, so the manifest version
     must be strictly greater than the base's.
   - `sw/version-bumped` — the change touches the publish set, so the version in `version_files`
     must be strictly greater than the base's.
2. **The release flows stop bumping.** Neither pipeline writes a version any more. Each releases the
   version it finds on `main`, and is a clean no-op when a release for that version already exists.
3. **The release flows can still bump deliberately** — a `workflow_dispatch` that raises the minor or
   major (extension) / the major (site) and pushes it, for the "new generation" statement that is not
   attached to any one change.

Owner decisions taken in the session that opened this:

- the extension's daily job stays, and runs the release flow when the version on `main` has not been
  released yet (rather than diffing shipped files);
- the site keeps `<major>.<ymmdd>.<n>` — a PR-time bump anchors the date to when the change was
  authored, which is the same day it deploys in practice.

name: "Chrome extension: Create Package (reusable)"

# Reusable workflow of the Chrome Web Store release standard — the logic behind
# every extension repo's release "create-package" job. Vendored into the
# extension repo by the chrome-extension pack (not hosted in Claudinite);
# the repo's single `chrome-extension-release.yml` orchestrator calls it locally
# (uses: ./.github/workflows/chrome-extension-create-package.yml) and passes NO
# repo values. workflow_call ONLY. All repo-specific values come from the
# caller's optional `.github/release.config` (read by the read-release-config
# composite action) plus the standard's defaults — the zip name is derived from
# the repo name, so a single-package repo needs no config at all.
#
# Builds and publishes a GitHub Release of the extension at the version that is
# currently committed in the extension manifest. It does NOT change the version —
# bumping is a deliberate, human step (ask Claude to "bump version"; it edits the
# manifest and package.json on a branch and lands on main via a normal PR — see
# the chrome-extension release standard in Claudinite).
#
# If the manifest version already matches the latest published release, the run
# is a clean no-op — so pushes to main that aren't version bumps don't cut a
# release. (The orchestrator triggers this on every push to main and relies on
# that no-op, so it needs no per-repo manifest path in its trigger.)
#
# The `ref` input exists for the daily auto-release
# (chrome-extension-daily-release.yml), which calls this after pushing its
# patch-bump commit: that run was triggered before the bump commit existed, so
# the default checkout (github.sha) would build the pre-bump tree and no-op on
# the old version.
#
# The calling job must grant `permissions: contents: write, issues: write`
# (release publishing + the failure reporter).
on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      ref:
        description: "Commit to release (blank = the commit that triggered the run)"
        required: false
        type: string
      build_env:
        description: >-
          Optional KEY=VALUE lines exported to the test/build steps (a repo that
          bakes release config from repository variables into its build passes
          them here). Every listed key must have a non-empty value or the run
          fails — so a mis-configured zip can't ship.
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ""

permissions:
  contents: write

# The implicit run shell has no pipefail; several steps pipe.
defaults:
  run:
    shell: bash

jobs:
  release:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
        with:
          # Empty (every caller but the daily-release) = the default
          # github.sha checkout.
          ref: ${{ inputs.ref }}

      # Resolve manifest_path / package_json_path / setup_command / test_command /
      # build_command / zip_path from the caller's .github/release.config (all
      # optional) + defaults; zip_name is derived from the repo name.
      - id: cfg
        uses: ./.github/actions/read-release-config

      - uses: actions/setup-node@v5
        with:
          node-version: 22
          # npm caching needs a lockfile; a repo that skips install has none.
          cache: ${{ steps.cfg.outputs.setup_command != '' && 'npm' || '' }}

      - name: Install dependencies
        if: steps.cfg.outputs.setup_command != ''
        run: ${{ steps.cfg.outputs.setup_command }}

      # Export the caller's release config and refuse to proceed on an empty
      # value — this is the generic form of "fail fast rather than ship a
      # placeholder-configured zip to the store".
      - name: Export and require the build env
        if: inputs.build_env != ''

# the repo's single `chrome-extension-release.yml` orchestrator calls it locally
# (uses: ./.github/workflows/chrome-extension-create-package.yml) and passes NO
# repo values. workflow_call ONLY. All repo-specific values come from the
# caller's optional `.github/release.config` (read by the read-release-config
# composite action) plus the standard's defaults — the zip name is derived from
# the repo name, so a single-package repo needs no config at all.
#
# Builds and publishes a GitHub Release of the extension at the version that is
# currently committed in the extension manifest. It does NOT change the version —
# bumping is a deliberate, human step (ask Claude to "bump version"; it edits the
# manifest and package.json on a branch and lands on main via a normal PR — see
# the chrome-extension release standard in Claudinite).
#
# If the manifest version already matches the latest published release, the run
# is a clean no-op — so pushes to main that aren't version bumps don't cut a
# release. (The orchestrator triggers this on every push to main and relies on
# that no-op, so it needs no per-repo manifest path in its trigger.)
#
# The `ref` input exists for the daily auto-release
# (chrome-extension-daily-release.yml), which calls this after pushing its
# patch-bump commit: that run was triggered before the bump commit existed, so
# the default checkout (github.sha) would build the pre-bump tree and no-op on
# the old version.
#
# The calling job must grant `permissions: contents: write, issues: write`
# (release publishing + the failure reporter).
on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      ref:
        description: "Commit to release (blank = the commit that triggered the run)"
        required: false
        type: string
      build_env:
        description: >-
          Optional KEY=VALUE lines exported to the test/build steps (a repo that
          bakes release config from repository variables into its build passes
          them here). Every listed key must have a non-empty value or the run
          fails — so a mis-configured zip can't ship.
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ""

permissions:
  contents: write

# The implicit run shell has no pipefail; several steps pipe.
defaults:
  run:
    shell: bash

jobs:
  release:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:

          # Empty (every caller but the daily-release) = the default
          # github.sha checkout.
          ref: ${{ inputs.ref }}

      # build_command / zip_path from the caller's .github/release.config (all

      # value — this is the generic form of "fail fast rather than ship a
      # placeholder-configured zip to the store".
      - name: Export and require the build env
        if: inputs.build_env != ''
        run: |
          while IFS= read -r line; do
            [ -z "$line" ] && continue

        id: version
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          MANIFEST_PATH: ${{ steps.cfg.outputs.manifest_path }}
          PACKAGE_JSON_PATH: ${{ steps.cfg.outputs.package_json_path }}
        run: |
          version="$(node -p "require('./$MANIFEST_PATH').version")"
          if ! echo "$version" | grep -Eq '^[0-9]+\.[0-9]+\.[0-9]+$'; then
            echo "$MANIFEST_PATH version '$version' is not X.Y.Z." >&2
            exit 1
          fi
          pkg_version="$(node -p "require('./$PACKAGE_JSON_PATH').version")"
          if [ "$pkg_version" != "$version" ]; then
            echo "$PACKAGE_JSON_PATH ($pkg_version) and $MANIFEST_PATH ($version) disagree — bump both together." >&2
            exit 1
          fi
          latest="$(gh release view --json tagName -q .tagName 2>/dev/null | sed 's/^v//' || true)"

            echo "v$version is already released; nothing to do." | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
            echo "release=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            exit 0
          fi
          echo "release=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "version=$version" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "tag=v$version" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "Releasing v$version" >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

        if: steps.version.outputs.release == 'true'
        run: ${{ steps.cfg.outputs.test_command }}

      # root `build` script that delegates), so it is mandated here, not a config
      # key. TWO zips come off the one tested tree, differing ONLY in the API
      # pointer that build_env's API_BASE_URL injects:
      #   * <zip>-prod.zip — the FULL injected config (API_BASE_URL → prod). This
      #     is the store's source of truth: the publish workflow downloads THIS
      #     asset. It is never the release's headline download.
      #   * <zip> — the SAME build with API_BASE_URL cleared, so config.mjs keeps
      #     its committed default (dev, by the standard's "no env ⇒ dev" rule). It

      #     …/releases/latest/download/<zip> URL — so what a human downloads and
      #     loads unpacked talks to DEV, never prod; only the store submission is
      #     prod-pointed. (API_BASE_URL is the standard's one dev/prod pointer key;

      #     keeps a stable id and working OAuth.)
      - name: Build the release zips (dev headline download + prod store artifact)
        id: build
        if: steps.version.outputs.release == 'true'
        env:
          ZIP_NAME: ${{ steps.cfg.outputs.zip_name }}
        run: |
          npm run build
          prod_zip="dist/${ZIP_NAME%.zip}-prod.zip"
          mv "dist/$ZIP_NAME" "$prod_zip"

      # branch protection on main doesn't apply. Both zips are attached: the dev
      # headline zip and the prod zip the store publish consumes.
      - name: Publish GitHub Release
        if: steps.version.outputs.release == 'true'
        uses: softprops/action-gh-release@v2
        with:
          tag_name: ${{ steps.version.outputs.tag }}
          target_commitish: ${{ inputs.ref || github.sha }}
          files: |
            ${{ steps.cfg.outputs.zip_path }}
            ${{ steps.build.outputs.prod_zip }}
          generate_release_notes: true

  # success, not failure, so it never reaches here.) The issue is keyed on the
  # standard's job name, stable across repos and callers.

    needs: release
    if: failure()
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      issues: write
    steps:
      - uses: ./.github/actions/report-failure
        with:
          workflow: "Release: Create Package"

input.content:
name: "Static site: Publish (reusable)"

# The logic behind every static-site repo's release, vendored from the
# static-website pack into the repo's own .github/. workflow_call ONLY — the
# `static-site-release.yml` orchestrator owns the triggers and passes no repo
# values; everything repo-specific comes from `.github/site.config` via the
# read-site-config composite action.
#
# THIS PIPELINE WRITES NO VERSION. The version belongs to the change that
# earned it: a PR touching the published site raises it in the same PR (the
# pack's `sw/version-bumped` check holds that line), so what reaches main is
# already the number to release. A deliberate generation bump — the major — is
# the orchestrator's `bump` dispatch, which pushes a bump and lets the ordinary
# push trigger release it.
#
# The pipeline, in order — and the order is the point: nothing is tagged or
# deployed until the tests that guard the site have passed.
#
#   check    is a release due? The version on main has no release of its own
#            yet — or `force`. Asking the RELEASE for the current version
#            (rather than diffing files against a tag) is what makes the flow
#            idempotent: a day whose run failed retries on the next push with
#            nothing to undo, and a push that only touched tooling carries the
#            same version and is a clean no-op.
#   verify   the repo's own gate (`test_command`), on the tree being released.
#   release  GitHub Release `v<major>.<ymmdd>.<n>` at that tree, with
#            auto-generated notes.
#   deploy   the Pages deploy of that exact commit, from the explicit publish
#            set.
#
# The caller must grant `permissions: contents: write, pages: write,
# id-token: write, issues: write`.
on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      force:
        description: "Release even when the version on main is already released"
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false

defaults:
  run:
    shell: bash

jobs:
  check:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
    outputs:
      release: ${{ steps.due.outputs.release }}
      version: ${{ steps.due.outputs.version }}
      released: ${{ steps.due.outputs.released }}
      test_command: ${{ steps.cfg.outputs.test_command }}
      sha: ${{ steps.head.outputs.sha }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
        with:
          # The branch tip as of now, not github.sha (the tip when the push
          # landed) — anything merged in between rides along in this release.
          ref: main
          # Full history + tags: the tag test below reads them.
          fetch-depth: 0

      # Pin that tip once, here: every later stage checks out THIS sha, so the
      # tree that is tested is the tree that is tagged and deployed.
      - id: head
        run: echo "sha=$(git rev-parse HEAD)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - id: cfg
        uses: ./.github/actions/read-site-config

      - name: Has the version on main been released yet?
        id: due
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          FORCE: ${{ inputs.force }}
          # Intentionally word-split below into the individual version records.
          VERSION_FILES: ${{ steps.cfg.outputs.version_files }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # The bump script is also the version READER, so nothing else has to
          # know how a repo's version record is shaped.
          version="$(node .github/actions/bump-site-version/bump.mjs --print $VERSION_FILES)"
          echo "version=$version" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          released=false
          if gh release view "v$version" >/dev/null 2>&1 || git rev-parse "v$version" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            released=true
          fi
          echo "released=$released" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          if [ "$released" = "false" ]; then
            echo "v$version is not released yet — releasing." | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
            echo "release=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          elif [ "$FORCE" = "true" ]; then
            echo "v$version is already released — forced, so redeploying it without a new tag." | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
            echo "release=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            echo "v$version is already released — nothing to do. Raise the version in the change that needs releasing." | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
            echo "release=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  # The repo's own gate, on the tree about to be released. Before the tag on
  # purpose: a failed gate must leave the tag and the live site exactly as they
  # were.
  verify:
    needs: check
    if: needs.check.outputs.release == 'true' && needs.check.outputs.test_command != ''
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
        with:
          ref: ${{ needs.check.outputs.sha }}
      # No install step and no npm cache: a test_command that needs dependencies
      # says so itself (`npm ci && npm test`), which keeps the config to the five
      # keys and never assumes a lockfile a plain HTML repo doesn't have.
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v5
        with:
          node-version: 22
      - name: Run the repo's gate
        run: ${{ needs.check.outputs.test_command }}

  release:
    needs: [check, verify]
    # `always()` so the skipped verify job (a repo that states test_command="")
    # does not skip the release with it; the explicit result test still stops a
    # real failure. A forced redeploy of an already-released version has nothing
    # to cut, so the job runs only for a version with no release of its own.
    if: >-
      always() && needs.check.outputs.release == 'true' &&
      needs.check.outputs.released == 'false' &&
      needs.verify.result != 'failure' && needs.verify.result != 'cancelled'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
        with:
          ref: ${{ needs.check.outputs.sha }}
          fetch-depth: 0
      - name: Cut the GitHub Release
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          VERSION: ${{ needs.check.outputs.version }}
          SHA: ${{ needs.check.outputs.sha }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          gh release create "v$VERSION" --target "$SHA" --title "v$VERSION" --generate-notes
          echo "Released v$VERSION." >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

  # The site itself, from the exact commit that was released.
  deploy:
    needs: [check, release]
    if: >-
      always() && needs.check.outputs.release == 'true' &&
      needs.release.result != 'failure' && needs.release.result != 'cancelled'
    permissions:
      contents: read
      pages: write
      id-token: write
    uses: ./.github/workflows/static-site-deploy-pages.yml
    with:
      ref: ${{ needs.check.outputs.sha }}

  # Release-on-push is unattended once the merge is done — a red run in the
  # Actions list reaches nobody. Converge any failure in this pipeline (its own
  # jobs and the called deploy alike) to a fresh tracking issue, superseding the
  # earlier open ones for this workflow so the newest failure is always the
  # single open bug to triage.
  report-failure:
    needs: [check, verify, release, deploy]
    if: failure()
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      issues: write
    steps:
      - name: Open a fresh failure issue and dedup earlier ones
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          RUN_URL: ${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}
          RUN_ID: ${{ github.run_id }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          prefix="⚠️ Workflow failing: Static site: Publish"
          title="${prefix} — $(date -u +%Y-%m-%d) (run ${RUN_ID})"
          # GitHub never creates a label on demand, and listing by a missing
          # label errors — so create it idempotently first.
          gh label create workflow-failure --repo "$REPO" --color B60205 \
            --description "An unattended workflow failed and needs a human" 2>/dev/null || true
          mapfile -t olds < <(gh issue list --repo "$REPO" --label workflow-failure \
            --state open --json number,title --limit 100 \
            -q "map(select(.title | startswith(\"$prefix\"))) | .[].number")
          url="$(gh issue create --repo "$REPO" --title "$title" --label workflow-failure \
            --body "The static-site release pipeline failed: [view run](${RUN_URL}). The site was NOT redeployed. Close this once the cause is fixed.")"
          new="${url##*/}"
          for n in "${olds[@]:-}"; do
            [ -n "$n" ] || continue
            gh issue comment "$n" --repo "$REPO" --body "Duplicate of #${new} — superseded by the latest failure of this workflow."

name: "Static site: Publish (reusable)"

# The logic behind every static-site repo's release, vendored from the
# static-website pack into the repo's own .github/. workflow_call ONLY — the
# `static-site-release.yml` orchestrator owns the triggers and passes no repo
# values; everything repo-specific comes from `.github/site.config` via the
# read-site-config composite action.
#
# THIS PIPELINE WRITES NO VERSION. The version belongs to the change that
# earned it: a PR touching the published site raises it in the same PR (the
# pack's `sw/version-bumped` check holds that line), so what reaches main is
# already the number to release. A deliberate generation bump — the major — is
# the orchestrator's `bump` dispatch, which pushes a bump and lets the ordinary
# push trigger release it.
#
# The pipeline, in order — and the order is the point: nothing is tagged or
# deployed until the tests that guard the site have passed.
#
#   check    is a release due? The version on main has no release of its own
#            yet — or `force`. Asking the RELEASE for the current version
#            (rather than diffing files against a tag) is what makes the flow
#            idempotent: a day whose run failed retries on the next push with
#            nothing to undo, and a push that only touched tooling carries the
#            same version and is a clean no-op.
#   verify   the repo's own gate (`test_command`), on the tree being released.
#   release  GitHub Release `v<major>.<ymmdd>.<n>` at that tree, with
#            auto-generated notes.
#   deploy   the Pages deploy of that exact commit, from the explicit publish
#            set.
#
# The caller must grant `permissions: contents: write, pages: write,
# id-token: write, issues: write`.
on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      force:
        description: "Release even when the version on main is already released"
        required: false
        type: boolean
        default: false

defaults:
  run:
    shell: bash

jobs:
  check:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
    outputs:
      release: ${{ steps.due.outputs.release }}
      version: ${{ steps.due.outputs.version }}
      released: ${{ steps.due.outputs.released }}
      test_command: ${{ steps.cfg.outputs.test_command }}
      sha: ${{ steps.head.outputs.sha }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
        with:
          # The branch tip as of now, not github.sha (the tip when the push
          # landed) — anything merged in between rides along in this release.
          ref: main
          # Full history + tags: the tag test below reads them.
          fetch-depth: 0

      # Pin that tip once, here: every later stage checks out THIS sha, so the
      # tree that is tested is the tree that is tagged and deployed.
      - id: head
        run: echo "sha=$(git rev-parse HEAD)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - id: cfg
        uses: ./.github/actions/read-site-config

      - name: Has the version on main been released yet?
        id: due
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          FORCE: ${{ inputs.force }}
          # Intentionally word-split below into the individual version records.
          VERSION_FILES: ${{ steps.cfg.outputs.version_files }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # The bump script is also the version READER, so nothing else has to
          # know how a repo's version record is shaped.
          version="$(node .github/actions/bump-site-version/bump.mjs --print $VERSION_FILES)"
          echo "version=$version" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          released=false
          if gh release view "v$version" >/dev/null 2>&1 || git rev-parse "v$version" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            released=true
          fi
          echo "released=$released" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          if [ "$released" = "false" ]; then
            echo "v$version is not released yet — releasing." | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
            echo "release=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          elif [ "$FORCE" = "true" ]; then
            echo "v$version is already released — forced, so redeploying it without a new tag." | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
            echo "release=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            echo "v$version is already released — nothing to do. Raise the version in the change that needs releasing." | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
            echo "release=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  # The repo's own gate, on the tree about to be released. Before the tag on
  # purpose: a failed gate must leave the tag and the live site exactly as they
  # were.
  verify:
    needs: check
    if: needs.check.outputs.release == 'true' && needs.check.outputs.test_command != ''
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
        with:
          ref: ${{ needs.check.outputs.sha }}
      # No install step and no npm cache: a test_command that needs dependencies
      # says so itself (`npm ci && npm test`), which keeps the config to the five
      # keys and never assumes a lockfile a plain HTML repo doesn't have.
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v5
        with:
          node-version: 22
      - name: Run the repo's gate
        run: ${{ needs.check.outputs.test_command }}

  release:
    needs: [check, verify]
    # `always()` so the skipped verify job (a repo that states test_command="")
    # does not skip the release with it; the explicit result test still stops a
    # real failure. A forced redeploy of an already-released version has nothing
    # to cut, so the job runs only for a version with no release of its own.
    if: >-
      always() && needs.check.outputs.release == 'true' &&
      needs.check.outputs.released == 'false' &&
      needs.verify.result != 'failure' && needs.verify.result != 'cancelled'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: write
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
        with:
          ref: ${{ needs.check.outputs.sha }}
          fetch-depth: 0
      - name: Cut the GitHub Release
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          VERSION: ${{ needs.check.outputs.version }}
          SHA: ${{ needs.check.outputs.sha }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          gh release create "v$VERSION" --target "$SHA" --title "v$VERSION" --generate-notes
          echo "Released v$VERSION." >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

  # The site itself, from the exact commit that was released.
  deploy:
    needs: [check, release]
    if: >-
      always() && needs.check.outputs.release == 'true' &&
      needs.release.result != 'failure' && needs.release.result != 'cancelled'
    permissions:
      contents: read
      pages: write
      id-token: write
    uses: ./.github/workflows/static-site-deploy-pages.yml
    with:
      ref: ${{ needs.check.outputs.sha }}

  # Release-on-push is unattended once the merge is done — a red run in the
  # Actions list reaches nobody. Converge any failure in this pipeline (its own
  # jobs and the called deploy alike) to a fresh tracking issue, superseding the
  # earlier open ones for this workflow so the newest failure is always the
  # single open bug to triage.
  report-failure:
    needs: [check, verify, release, deploy]
    if: failure()
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      issues: write
    steps:
      - name: Open a fresh failure issue and dedup earlier ones
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ github.token }}
          REPO: ${{ github.repository }}
          RUN_URL: ${{ github.server_url }}/${{ github.repository }}/actions/runs/${{ github.run_id }}
          RUN_ID: ${{ github.run_id }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          prefix="⚠️ Workflow failing: Static site: Publish"
          title="${prefix} — $(date -u +%Y-%m-%d) (run ${RUN_ID})"
          # GitHub never creates a label on demand, and listing by a missing
          # label errors — so create it idempotently first.
          gh label create workflow-failure --repo "$REPO" --color B60205 \
            --description "An unattended workflow failed and needs a human" 2>/dev/null || true
          mapfile -t olds < <(gh issue list --repo "$REPO" --label workflow-failure \
            --state open --json number,title --limit 100 \
            -q "map(select(.title | startswith(\"$prefix\"))) | .[].number")
          url="$(gh issue create --repo "$REPO" --title "$title" --label workflow-failure \
            --body "The static-site release pipeline failed: [view run](${RUN_URL}). The site was NOT redeployed. Close this once the cause is fixed.")"
          new="${url##*/}"
          for n in "${olds[@]:-}"; do
            [ -n "$n" ] || continue
            gh issue comment "$n" --repo "$REPO" --body "Duplicate of #${new} — superseded by the latest failure of this workflow."
            gh issue close "$n" --repo "$REPO" --reason "not planned" 2>/dev/null || gh issue close "$n" --repo "$REPO"
          done

name: "Static site: Bump version (reusable)"

# The DELIBERATE version bump, vendored from the static-website pack into the
# repo's own .github/. workflow_call ONLY — the `static-site-release.yml`
# orchestrator owns the trigger.
#
# This is the pipeline's ONLY write to a version, and it is never automatic. The
# routine bump belongs to the change that earned it: a PR touching the published
# site raises the version in the same PR, and `sw/version-bumped` is what holds
# that line. What is left over is the generation statement — "this is a new site"
# — which belongs to no single change, so a human dispatches it here.
#
# The date-anchored scheme has no minor: `<major>.<ymmdd>.<n>` computes its last
# two parts, so the major is the only part anyone chooses. Raising it restarts
# the day counter at today.

name: Release static site

# THE ORCHESTRATOR of the static-website release standard — the one entry point
# every static-site repo of ours carries, vendored from the pack into this repo's
# own .github/ (GitHub resolves a reusable workflow or composite action only from
# the repo's own .github/, never from a mount). It owns the TRIGGERS and nothing
# else: the logic lives in the local reusable workflows it calls, and every
# repo-specific value comes from this repo's `.github/site.config` (read inside
# those workflows), so this file is copy-verbatim in every site repo.
#
# Release on push: any push to main whose version has not been released yet cuts
# a release — tag it, deploy the site. The version comes from the CHANGE, not
# from here: a PR touching the published site raises it in the same PR
# (`sw/version-bumped`), so an ordinary README or tooling commit carries the
# version that is already out and is a clean no-op.
#
# The dispatch form has two knobs, and they compose:
#   * bump: major  — the deliberate "new generation of the site" statement, the
#                    one version write this pipeline still performs. It pushes
#                    the bump to main and then releases it.
#   * force: true  — release even when the version on main is already released
#                    (a rebuild after a settings fix, a first deploy on a repo
#                    whose site predates the pipeline). Redeploys the existing
#                    tag rather than cutting a second one.
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      bump:
        description: "Raise the version before releasing"
        type: choice
        options: [none, major]
        default: none
      force:
        description: "Release even when the version on main is already released"
        type: boolean
        default: false

# One release at a time, and never cancel one mid-flight: a cancelled run can
# leave the version bumped with no release or deploy behind it.
concurrency:
  group: static-site-release
  cancel-in-progress: false

jobs:
  # Dispatch-only, and only when asked for. The push trigger never reaches it,
  # so nothing writes a version unattended.
  bump:
    if: inputs.bump == 'major'
    permissions:
      contents: write
    uses: ./.github/workflows/static-site-bump-version.yml

  release:
    needs: bump
    # `always()` so the skipped bump job (every push, and every dispatch that
    # asked for no bump) does not skip the release with it; the explicit result
    # test still stops a failed bump from releasing a half-written version.
    if: always() && needs.bump.result != 'failure' && needs.bump.result != 'cancelled'
    permissions:
      contents: write   # create the release
      pages: write      # deploy the site
      id-token: write   # the OIDC token deploy-pages exchanges
      issues: write     # the failure reporter
    uses: ./.github/workflows/static-site-publish.yml
    with:
      force: ${{ inputs.force || false }}

name: "Chrome extension: Daily Auto-Release (reusable)"

# Reusable workflow of the Chrome Web Store release standard — the logic behind
# every extension repo's daily release. Vendored into the extension repo by the
# chrome-extension pack (not hosted in Claudinite); the repo's single
# `chrome-extension-release.yml` orchestrator owns the schedule/dispatch triggers
# and the `concurrency: daily-release` guard, calls this locally, and passes NO
# repo values. workflow_call ONLY. Everything repo-specific comes from the
# caller's `.github/release.config` (via the read-release-config composite
# action) — including the manifest that carries the version.
#
# THIS WORKFLOW WRITES NO VERSION. The version belongs to the change that earned
# it: a PR touching a shipped file raises the patch in the same PR (the pack's
# `cer/version-bumped` check holds that line), so what reaches main is already
# the number to ship. A deliberate minor or major is the orchestrator's `bump`
# dispatch.
#
# So "is a release due?" is one question, asked of the release list rather than
# of a file diff: has the version currently on main been released yet? That is
# self-healing by construction — a day whose run failed retries the next day with
# nothing to undo, a push that touched only tooling carries the version that is
# already out and is a clean no-op, and there is no window in which the pipeline
# and the repo disagree about what "the current version" is.
#
# When a release is due it:
#   1. calls the "Chrome extension: Create Package" reusable workflow (tests →
#      zip → GitHub Release) on main's tip. Called with an explicit ref because
#      the schedule fired against whatever main was then.
#   2. calls the "Chrome extension: Publish to Chrome Web Store" reusable
#      workflow with the fresh tag (auto-publishing to users, and refreshing
#      the privacy page as that workflow always does).
#
# Unattended (scheduled), so failures must reach a human: the called workflows
# report their own job failures as fresh tracking issues, and the
# report-failure job below covers this workflow's own jobs — including a
# called workflow failing to even start.
#
# The check job runs on a bare runner (no npm ci): the config action and the
# version read are dependency-free node. Callers must pass `secrets: inherit`
# (for the store secrets the publish leg needs) and grant `permissions:
# contents: write, pages: write, id-token: write, issues: write`.
on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      build_env:
        description: "Forwarded to the release workflow (KEY=VALUE lines; see there)"
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ""

defaults:
  run:
    shell: bash

jobs:
  check:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
    outputs:
      release: ${{ steps.due.outputs.release }}
      version: ${{ steps.due.outputs.version }}
      sha: ${{ steps.head.outputs.sha }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
        with:
          # The branch tip as of now, not github.sha (the tip when the schedule
          # fired) — anything merged in between rides along in this release.
          ref: main
          # Full history + tags: the tag test below reads them.
          fetch-depth: 0

      # Pin that tip once, here: the release is cut at THIS sha, so the tree
      # whose version was read is the tree that ships.
      - id: head
        run: echo "sha=$(git rev-parse HEAD)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"

      - id: cfg
        uses: ./.github/actions/read-release-config

      - name: Has the version on main been released yet?
        id: due
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          MANIFEST_PATH: ${{ steps.cfg.outputs.manifest_path }}
        run: |
          set -euo pipefail
          # The bump script is also the version READER, so nothing else has to
          # know where the version lives.
          version="$(node .github/actions/bump-extension-patch/bump.mjs --print "$MANIFEST_PATH")"
          echo "version=$version" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          if gh release view "v$version" >/dev/null 2>&1 || git rev-parse "v$version" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            echo "v$version is already released — nothing to ship. Raise the version in the change that needs shipping." | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
            echo "release=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            echo "v$version is not released yet — shipping it." | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
            echo "release=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  # Tests → zip → GitHub Release, at main's pinned tip. Its internal
  # report-failure job needs issues: write granted through this call.
  release:
    needs: check
    if: needs.check.outputs.release == 'true'
    permissions:
      contents: write
      issues: write
    uses: ./.github/workflows/chrome-extension-create-package.yml
    with:
      ref: ${{ needs.check.outputs.sha }}
      build_env: ${{ inputs.build_env }}

  # Upload the just-released zip to the Chrome Web Store and publish it to
  # users. secrets: inherit passes the four CHROME_* store secrets through;
  # the pages/id-token grants are for its privacy-page deploy, issues for the
  # nested failure reporters. The publish workflow reads the zip name from the
  # repo's release config itself, so only the tag is forwarded here.
  publish:
    needs: [check, release]
    permissions:
      contents: read
      pages: write
      id-token: write
      issues: write
    uses: ./.github/workflows/chrome-extension-publish-store.yml
    with:
      tag: v${{ needs.check.outputs.version }}
      auto_publish: true
    secrets: inherit

  # Scheduled + nobody watching = every failure must converge to a fresh
  # tracking issue a human sees. Covering release/publish here too can
  # double-report (their internal reporters also fire on their own job failures)
  # — accepted, so that a called workflow failing before its internal reporter
  # can run (e.g. a workflow-file error) still reaches a human.
  report-failure:
    needs: [check, release, publish]
    if: failure()
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      issues: write
    steps:
      - uses: ./.github/actions/report-failure
        with:
          workflow: "Release: Daily Auto-Release"

name: "Chrome extension: Daily Auto-Release (reusable)"

# Reusable workflow of the Chrome Web Store release standard — the logic behind
# every extension repo's daily release. Vendored into the extension repo by the
# chrome-extension pack (not hosted in Claudinite); the repo's single
# `chrome-extension-release.yml` orchestrator owns the schedule/dispatch triggers
# and the `concurrency: daily-release` guard, calls this locally, and passes NO
# repo values. workflow_call ONLY. Everything repo-specific comes from the
# caller's optional `.github/release.config` (via the read-release-config
# composite action) plus defaults — including the shipped-file set (`ship_paths`)
# and the version files the patch bump edits (`manifest_path`/`package_json_path`),
# so no repo carries a bump or filter script any more.
#
# Ships the extension to the Chrome Web Store once a day — but only when
# something DEPLOYABLE changed. "Deployable" = a change under one of the repo's
# `ship_paths` (default: the extension directory; a repo that ships a curated
# subset lists the roots and a repo test keeps them honest against its build).
#
# The baseline is the LATEST PUBLISHED RELEASE TAG, not a literal 24-hour
# window: on a daily schedule the two are normally the same set of commits, but
# the tag baseline is self-healing — a day whose run failed (or a change older
# than a day that never shipped) is still caught the next day instead of
# stranded.
#
# When a release is due it:
#   1. patch-bumps the version (the canon bump-extension-patch action — the
#      manifest and package.json together) and pushes the bump to main, because
#      the store rejects an upload whose version isn't strictly higher than the
#      live one. Deliberate human bumps ("bump version", default minor) are
#      unaffected.
#   2. calls the "Chrome extension: Create Package" reusable workflow (tests →
#      zip → GitHub Release) on the bump commit. Called explicitly because the
#      bump was pushed with GITHUB_TOKEN, which never fires the caller stub's
#      push trigger.
#   3. calls the "Chrome extension: Publish to Chrome Web Store" reusable
#      workflow with the fresh tag (auto-publishing to users, and refreshing
#      the privacy page as that workflow always does).
#
# Unattended (scheduled), so failures must reach a human: the called workflows
# report their own job failures as fresh tracking issues, and the
# report-failure job below covers this workflow's own jobs — including a
# called workflow failing to even start.
#
# The check/bump jobs run on a bare runner (no npm ci): the config action and
# the bump action are dependency-free node, and the change filter is pure bash.
# Callers must pass `secrets: inherit` (for the store secrets the publish leg
# needs) and grant `permissions: contents: write, pages: write, id-token: write,
# issues: write`.
on:
  workflow_call:
    inputs:
      build_env:
        description: "Forwarded to the release workflow (KEY=VALUE lines; see there)"
        required: false
        type: string
        default: ""

defaults:
  run:
    shell: bash

jobs:
  check:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: read
    outputs:
      release: ${{ steps.diff.outputs.release }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
        with:
          # Full history + tags: the diff below is against the latest release tag.
          fetch-depth: 0

      - id: cfg
        uses: ./.github/actions/read-release-config

      - name: Look for shipped-file changes since the last release
        id: diff
        env:
          GH_TOKEN: ${{ secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN }}
          SHIP_PATHS: ${{ steps.cfg.outputs.ship_paths }}
        run: |
          latest="$(gh release view --json tagName -q .tagName 2>/dev/null || true)"
          if [ -z "$latest" ]; then
            echo "No published release to diff against — releasing the current tree." | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
            echo "release=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
            exit 0
          fi
          # Keep only changed paths under one of the shipped roots ($SHIP_PATHS
          # is intentionally word-split into space-separated roots). A root can
          # be a directory ("extension") or an exact file ("extension/manifest.json").
          changed=""
          while IFS= read -r f; do
            [ -z "$f" ] && continue
            for root in $SHIP_PATHS; do
              case "$f" in
                "$root"|"$root"/*) changed="${changed}${f}"$'\n'; break;;
              esac
            done
          done < <(git diff --name-only "$latest" HEAD)
          if [ -z "$changed" ]; then
            echo "No shipped-file changes since $latest — nothing to release." | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
            echo "release=false" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          else
            { echo "Shipped files changed since $latest — releasing:"; printf '%s' "$changed"; } | tee -a "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"
            echo "release=true" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          fi

  # The store needs a strictly-higher version, so the release starts with a
  # patch bump pushed straight to main (this workflow's one deliberate
  # exception to bumps-are-a-human-PR — see the chrome-extension release
  # standard in Claudinite). If main moved between checkout and push the push
  # fails non-fast-forward; that's a loud red the reporter turns into an issue,
  # and the next day's run catches everything up.
  bump:
    needs: check
    if: needs.check.outputs.release == 'true'
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      contents: write
    outputs:
      version: ${{ steps.bump.outputs.version }}
      sha: ${{ steps.push.outputs.sha }}
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v5
        with:
          # The branch tip as of now, not github.sha (the tip when the schedule
          # fired) — anything merged in between rides along in this release.
          ref: main

      - id: cfg
        uses: ./.github/actions/read-release-config

      - id: bump
        uses: ./.github/actions/bump-extension-patch
        with:
          manifest_path: ${{ steps.cfg.outputs.manifest_path }}
          package_json_path: ${{ steps.cfg.outputs.package_json_path }}

      - name: Push the bump to main
        id: push
        run: |
          git config user.name "github-actions[bot]"
          git config user.email "41898282+github-actions[bot]@users.noreply.github.com"
          git commit -am "Bump version to ${{ steps.bump.outputs.version }} (daily auto-release) [skip ci]"
          git push origin HEAD:main
          echo "sha=$(git rev-parse HEAD)" >> "$GITHUB_OUTPUT"
          echo "Bumped to v${{ steps.bump.outputs.version }}." >> "$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY"

  # Tests → zip → GitHub Release, on the bump commit (see the ref input's note
  # in chrome-extension-create-package.yml). Its internal report-failure job
  # needs issues: write granted through this call.
  release:
    needs: bump
    permissions:
      contents: write
      issues: write
    uses: ./.github/workflows/chrome-extension-create-package.yml
    with:
      ref: ${{ needs.bump.outputs.sha }}
      build_env: ${{ inputs.build_env }}

  # Upload the just-released zip to the Chrome Web Store and publish it to
  # users. secrets: inherit passes the four CHROME_* store secrets through;
  # the pages/id-token grants are for its privacy-page deploy, issues for the
  # nested failure reporters. The publish workflow reads the zip name from the
  # repo's release config itself, so only the tag is forwarded here.
  publish:
    needs: [bump, release]
    permissions:
      contents: read
      pages: write
      id-token: write
      issues: write
    uses: ./.github/workflows/chrome-extension-publish-store.yml
    with:
      tag: v${{ needs.bump.outputs.version }}
      auto_publish: true
    secrets: inherit

  # Scheduled + nobody watching = every failure must converge to a fresh
  # tracking issue a human sees. Covering release/publish here too can
  # double-report (their internal reporters also fire on their own job failures)
  # — accepted, so that a called workflow failing before its internal reporter
  # can run (e.g. a workflow-file error) still reaches a human.
  report-failure:
    needs: [check, bump, release, publish]
    if: failure()
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    permissions:
      issues: write
    steps:
      - uses: ./.github/actions/report-failure
        with:
          workflow: "Release: Daily Auto-Release"

# publish, and the deliberate version bump — lives in the reusable workflows this
# repo carries alongside it in `.github/workflows/` (all vendored from the
# chrome-extension pack, so they run entirely inside this repo — no cross-repo
# `@main` dependency). This file passes NO repo values. Every repo-specific value
# is declared explicitly in the REQUIRED `.github/release.config` (five keys, no
# defaults) — the pack keeps this whole set (`.github/workflows/` +
# `.github/actions/`) in sync, so treat it as generated: edit the pack, not the
# copy. The zip asset name is derived from the config's `zip_path`, and the build
# is always `npm run build`, so neither is a config key.
#
# THE VERSION COMES FROM THE CHANGE. A PR touching a shipped file raises the
# patch in the same PR (`cer/version-bumped`), so merging it is what cuts the
# release: create-package no-ops unless the version on main has no release yet.
# Nothing here bumps on its own; `mode: bump` is the deliberate minor/major, run
# by a human.
#
# Four operations, one entry point:
#   * push to main            → create-package (a clean no-op unless the version
#                               was raised, so ordinary pushes don't cut a
#                               release — no per-repo manifest path in the trigger)
#   * schedule (00:30 UTC)    → daily auto-release (ship the version on main to
#                               the store if it has not been released yet)
#   * "Run workflow" dispatch → pick a mode: publish (default), package, daily,
#                               or bump (with `part`, minor or major — raises the
#                               version, pushes it, and packages the result)
#
# The Actions-tab entry is named "Release to Chrome Store"; the failure reporter keys its
# tracking issues on the per-operation names ("Release: Create Package", etc.)
# baked into the reusable workflows, so collapsing to one entry point loses no
# per-operation triage.
#
# secrets: inherit passes the four CHROME_* store secrets through to the reusable
# workflows.
#
# A repo whose build bakes in per-environment config (e.g. an API base URL)
# uncomments a build_env block on the create-package and daily jobs — the ONLY
# place a repo references its repository variables; every key must be non-empty
# or the run fails, so a mis-configured zip can't ship. Example:
#       build_env: |
#         API_BASE_URL=${{ vars.API_BASE_URL }}
on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  schedule:
    - cron: "30 0 * * *"
  workflow_dispatch:
    inputs:
      mode:
        description: "What to run"
        type: choice
        options: [publish, package, daily, bump]
        default: publish
      part:
        description: "bump: which part to raise"
        type: choice
        options: [minor, major]
        default: minor
      tag:
        description: "publish: release tag to publish (blank = latest release)"
        required: false
        type: string
      auto_publish:
        description: "publish: publish to users after upload (uncheck = dashboard draft)"
        type: boolean
        default: true

permissions:
  contents: write
  pages: write
  id-token: write
  issues: write

# Daily runs (scheduled, or a mode=daily dispatch) share one queue so a manual
# dispatch can't race the scheduled release; every other run gets its own group.
concurrency: >-
  ${{ (github.event_name == 'schedule' ||
       (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.mode == 'daily'))
      && 'daily-release' || github.run_id }}

jobs:
  # Dispatch-only, and only when asked for. Neither the push nor the schedule
  # reaches it, so nothing writes a version unattended.
  bump:
    if: github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.mode == 'bump'
    permissions:
      contents: write
    uses: ./.github/workflows/chrome-extension-bump-version.yml
    with:
      part: ${{ inputs.part }}

  create-package:
    needs: bump
    # `always()` so the skipped bump job (every push, and every dispatch that
    # asked for something else) does not skip the package with it; the explicit
    # result test still stops a failed bump from releasing a half-written
    # version. The bump's push used GITHUB_TOKEN and fired no trigger, so its
    # commit is passed here by sha.
    if: >-
      always() && needs.bump.result != 'failure' && needs.bump.result != 'cancelled' &&
      (github.event_name == 'push' ||
       (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && (inputs.mode == 'package' || inputs.mode == 'bump')))
    uses: ./.github/workflows/chrome-extension-create-package.yml
    with:
      ref: ${{ needs.bump.outputs.sha }}
    # build_env: uncomment on this job and `daily` if the build needs repo config
    #   with:
    #     build_env: |
    #       API_BASE_URL=${{ vars.API_BASE_URL }}

  publish:
    if: github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.mode == 'publish'
    uses: ./.github/workflows/chrome-extension-publish-store.yml
    with:
      tag: ${{ inputs.tag }}
      auto_publish: ${{ inputs.auto_publish }}
    secrets: inherit

  daily:
    if: >-
      github.event_name == 'schedule' ||
      (github.event_name == 'workflow_dispatch' && inputs.mode == 'daily')
    uses: ./.github/workflows/chrome-extension-daily-release.yml
    secrets: inherit

## The contract

**Versioning**

- The extension manifest's `version` (`X.Y.Z`) is the single source of truth. The extension's
  `package.json` `version` must equal it, enforced by a CI-run guard (a unit test or an inline
  workflow check — the repo picks the mechanism, the invariant is fixed).
- Minor/major bumps are deliberate and human: **"bump version"** = edit the manifest and
  `package.json` (plus any repo version-sync constant) together on a branch — default the next
  **minor** — and land on `main` via a normal PR. Merging the bump *is* cutting the release.
- Patch bumps belong to the daily auto-release. No workflow other than the daily bump ever
  changes the version; "Release: Create Package" never does.

**Artifact**

…
`Release to Chrome Store`. It owns only the triggers; its three `if:`-guarded jobs each call a **local**
reusable workflow (`./.github/workflows/…`, all vendored alongside it). The failure reporter keys
tracking issues on the **per-operation** names baked into the reusable workflows (`Release: Create
Package`, `Release: Publish to Chrome Web Store`, `Release: Daily Auto-Release`) — not on the
orchestrator's `name:` — so collapsing to one entry point loses no per-operation triage:

| job (trigger) | reusable workflow it calls — what it does |
|---|---|
| `create-package` (push to `main`; dispatch `mode: package`) | `chrome-extension-create-package.yml` — version guard (a clean no-op unless the manifest version was bumped, so ordinary pushes don't cut a release) → full test gate → build the dev headline `<zip>` + the prod `<zip>-prod.zip` → GitHub Release |
| `publish` (dispatch `mode: publish` — the default — with `tag`, `auto_publish`) | `chrome-extension-publish-store.yml` — download the prod `<zip>-prod.zip` (falls back to `<zip>` for pre-split releases) → upload via the store API (publish to users unless `auto_publish: false` → dashboard draft) → refresh the `/privacy/` page (via the `deploy-privacy-page.yml` reusable) |
| `daily` (schedule `30 0 * * *`; dispatch `mode: daily`) | `chrome-extension-daily-release.yml` — shipped-file diff vs the latest release tag → patch bump pushed to `main` → calls the two reusable workflows above |

The `create-package` job triggers on **every** push to `main` (no per-repo manifest path in the
trigger) and relies on the version guard to no-op unless a bump landed. The privacy page has **no

# Static website

A static site that releases on push and serves from GitHub Pages. The full contract — the pipeline, the config, the setup — is [the static-site-releases skill](skills/static-site-releases/SKILL.md); these are the things a session touching such a repo has to know before it edits anything.

- **A published file is a file the publish set names — adding a page is two edits.** The Pages artifact is assembled from `.github/site.config`'s `publish_paths` and nothing else, so a new page, stylesheet or data file that isn't under a published path (or named in the list) is simply absent from the live site, with no error anywhere: the build is green, the deploy succeeds, the page 404s. When you add a file the site serves, put it under an already-published directory or add it to `publish_paths` in the same change. The list is additive on purpose — the alternative, "publish the repo minus what we remember to exclude", publishes every draft, note and key nobody thought to hide.
- **The version moves with the change that ships it.** A change touching the published site raises `<major>.<ymmdd>.<n>` in the same PR — `node .github/actions/bump-site-version/bump.mjs $(version_files)` computes it from the previous version and the UTC date, and `sw/version-bumped` is what holds the line. Never hand-write the `ymmdd` or the counter: a typed value either collides with a released one or is dated in the future, and the next bump refuses. The release flow writes no version of its own — it ships what it finds on `main` — so a shipped change without a bump is never released at all. The one deliberate human part is the **major**, a "this is a new generation of the site" statement; the owner's **"bump version"** means exactly that, and the release workflow's `bump: major` dispatch is what performs it.
- **The pipeline files under `.github/workflows/static-site-*` and `.github/actions/{read-site-config,bump-site-version,assemble-site}` are managed copies of the pack's `stubs/`.** Fix the pack and re-vendor; an edit to the copy is overwritten and, until it is, makes this repo's pipeline differ from every other site repo's. The repo's own values all live in `.github/site.config`, which is what the copies read.
- **The site is served from a subpath, not a domain root.** GitHub Pages serves it at `https://<owner>.github.io/<repo>/` (unless a custom domain is configured), so a root-relative URL — `/style.css`, `/img/logo.png`, a `fetch('/data.json')` — resolves above the site and 404s in production while working fine in a local `file://` or `python -m http.server` preview. Write links, asset paths and fetches **relative** to the page.
