sections. This skill is that contract, the setup steps for a new extension repo, and the manual
Chrome Web Store actions the automation can't do. The workflow **logic** is authored once, in this
pack's [`stubs/`](../../stubs/) — the [orchestrator](../../stubs/workflows/chrome-extension-release.yml), the
four `workflow_call`-only **reusable workflows**, and the
[report-failure](../../stubs/actions/report-failure/action.yml),
[read-release-config](../../stubs/actions/read-release-config/action.yml) and
[bump-extension-patch](../../stubs/actions/bump-extension-patch/action.yml) composite actions — and
**vendored into each extension repo's own `.github/`**, where the whole pipeline runs with no
cross-repo dependency. GitHub only resolves a reusable workflow or composite action from a repo's
own `.github/`, so "the logic lives in the pack" means the pack holds the templates and each repo
hosts a *managed* copy: the pack keeps every copy in sync — baselining re-materializes on drift via
the `chrome-release-vendoring` migration — so a repo **hosts** the pipeline without **owning** it.
Treat the vendored `.github/workflows/` + `.github/actions/` set as generated: edit the pack, not
the copy. A repo adds only its **required** `.github/release.config` (five explicit keys, **no
defaults**). A merged canon change reaches every extension repo through the nightly baselining, not
a live `@main` reference. Everything a repo used to carry as workflow values — the version files, the
zip location, the test gate, the shipping set, and the previously per-repo `bump`/`filter` scripts
— is either pack logic (the bump/filter, and `npm run build`) or an explicit `release.config` key,
so no repo ships a bump or filter script any more. Reference implementation:
`missingbulb/GoogleCalendarEventCreator`; also adopted by `TLDR` and `CrosswordChat`.

input.body:
Closes #1150.

## The problem

Both release standards wrote the version themselves — the extension's daily run patch-bumped and
pushed to `main` before packaging, the site's publish reusable computed `<major>.<ymmdd>.<n>` and
pushed it before tagging. So the version a reviewer saw on a PR was never the version that shipped,
and the one push a pipeline made to `main` unattended was the one that could fail non-fast-forward
and strand a release. Claudinite holds the opposite line on itself — `pack-version-bumped`,
`engine-release-record`. These two packs now hold it too.

## What lands

**A work-scope check per pack**, gated on the repo shipping the pipeline and scoped by the repo's
own declaration of what ships:

| check | fires when |
|---|---|
| `cer/version-bumped` | the change touches something under `ship_paths` and the manifest version did not rise |
| `sw/version-bumped` | the change touches the publish set and `version_files` did not rise |

Both are silent on a change that ships nothing (a README, a test, a workflow), and both defer to the
neighbouring check (`cer/version-sync`, `sw/version-scheme`) on an off-scheme version rather than
reporting it twice.

**The pipelines stop writing versions.** Each now asks the release list whether the version on `main`
has been released yet, rather than diffing files against a tag — idempotent by construction, so a
failed run retries with nothing to undo and a push carrying an already-released version is a clean
no-op. The extension's `create-package` already worked this way; the daily run just loses its `bump`
job.

**The deliberate bump stays, as a dispatch**, because it belongs to no single change: `mode: bump`
with `part: minor|major` on the extension orchestrator, `bump: major` on the site's (the
date-anchored scheme has no minor). Each calls a new vendored reusable that raises the version,
pushes it, and lets the ordinary release path ship it.

Owner decisions taken in the session: the extension's daily job stays and releases when the version
on `main` has not been released yet; the site keeps `<major>.<ymmdd>.<n>`, so a PR-time bump anchors
the date to when the change was authored.

## Folders touched

```
packs/chrome-extension/
  cer/version-bumped (new work rule) + its tests; the daily reusable loses its bump job and
  asks the release list instead; a new chrome-extension-bump-version.yml reusable; the
  orchestrator gains mode: bump / part; bump.mjs gains minor/major/--print/compare and becomes
  importable; read-release-config exports a pure parse for the check to share; pack version,
  vendored-file lists, migration materialize list, README catalog row, and the release standard.

packs/static-website/
  sw/version-bumped (new work rule) + its tests; the publish reusable loses its bump job and
  asks the release list instead; a new static-site-bump-version.yml reusable; the orchestrator
  gains bump: major; bump.mjs gains --major/--print/compare; pack version, vendored-file lists,
  migration materialize list, RULES.md version rule, README catalog rows, and the release standard.
  Separately: the standing vendoring record now materializes export-build-vars.mjs, which it had
  been omitting — a repo declaring build_vars could not self-heal onto a copy that honours it.

packs/basics/
  the bump-version skill reads for a world where the patch is the change's own — what is left
  to ask for is the minor or the major.

engine-tests/
  the chrome vendoring round-trip counts one more workflow.
```

## Verification

- `node --test $(git ls-files '*.test.mjs')` — 2390 tests, one failure, pre-existing and
  environmental (`engine-pack-lane-shims` refuses to run against this sandbox's shallow clone).
- `check_the_world` — 0 blocking, 71 advisory, byte-identical to `main`'s output.
- `check_the_work --changed` — clean.
- Both new checks were written failing-case first; their tests assert the finding's file, severity
  and wording on the miss, and silence on each of the deliberately-free cases.

## Not covered

The canon's own dead `.github/actions/bump-extension-patch/` and `.github/workflows/chrome-extension-*`
copies — the pre-vendoring core plumbing the vendoring migration's header says stays until someone
sweeps it by hand — are left as they are and now differ from the pack's stubs. Nothing executes them.

**What the two new checks do**

| check | fires when | silent on |
|---|---|---|
| [`cer/version-bumped`](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/blob/claude/version-bump-checks-r43gr9/packs/chrome-extension/version-bumped.mjs) | the diff touches something under `ship_paths` and the manifest version didn't rise | README/test/workflow changes, a repo that doesn't ship, an off-scheme version (that's `cer/version-sync`'s) |
| [`sw/version-bumped`](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/blob/claude/version-bump-checks-r43gr9/packs/static-website/version-bumped.mjs) | the diff touches the publish set and `version_files` didn't rise | same shape; off-scheme is `sw/version-scheme`'s |

Each reads the repo's *own* declaration of what ships, so the check's scope and the release trigger's scope are one statement, not two.

**The release flows** stopped writing versions entirely. Both now ask the release list "has the version on `main` been released yet?" instead of diffing files against a tag — which is what makes them idempotent: a failed run retries with nothing to undo, and a push carrying an already-released version no-ops. What's left is the bump that belongs to no single change, and each orchestrator got a dispatch for it: `mode: bump` + `part: minor|major` on the extension, `bump: major` on the site (its date-anchored scheme has no minor).

Two judgment calls worth your eye:

- The chrome bump action keeps its `bump-extension-patch` path even though it now writes any part. It's vendored into every extension repo and migration records have no delete verb, so a rename would strand the old directory in each of them — the same call the `cer/` prefix already carries, with the reason at the site.
- I fixed an unrelated gap I ran into: the static-site vendoring record wasn't materializing `export-build-vars.mjs`, so a repo declaring `build_vars` hit a blocking finding it could only clear by hand. Split into its own commit.

Full suite: 2390 tests, one pre-existing environmental failure (`engine-pack-lane-shims` refuses this sandbox's shallow clone). `check_the_world` is byte-identical to `main`'s 0 blocking / 71 advisory; `check_the_work` clean.

> ⚠️ Still open: [#1151](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/1151) awaits your review. Nothing is verified in production yet — the checks and the pipelines only prove out once a real extension or site repo takes the vendored copies, which is the nightly converge's job.

# Owner interaction preferences

Personal preferences from the repo owner for how the assistant should interact — tone, summary style, end-of-turn conventions, how results and decisions are surfaced, and the phrases the owner uses to trigger defined commands. These are **not** project conventions (those live in the [packs/](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/tree/main/packs) corpus, each pack bundling its skills); they're how the owner likes to be worked with. Where a preference triggers a command whose mechanics are a project convention, the mechanics stay in their own doc and the entry here just owns the trigger phrase.

## Preferences

- **End every turn with a blockquote callout** — `> ✅ All done`, or `> ⚠️ Still open: …` listing what remains — never hedged in prose.
- **"LGTM"** merges the change at hand into `main` (`merge-to-main` skill); it approves that change only, never later work.
- **"bump version"** raises the project's version; the project's own workflow decides how it changes and which files change.
- **In the conversation**: link every source-controlled document you edit, display every image you edit, link every issue/PR number.
- **Ask every decision or approval through an `AskUserQuestion` popup, never prose** — one question per item, each with its case.
- **Enclose anything the owner will lift elsewhere** — a prompt, a message, copy to paste — in one delimited block, boundaries unmistakable.
- **Prefix a prompt for another session, inside its block, with a disclaimer**: Claude wrote it — examine inconsistencies, don't follow blindly.
- **Open a pull request right after committing to a branch**, unasked — overriding Claude Code's default of waiting to be told.
- **When handing over a PR to review, describe the folders the change touched in the conversation, in a text box** — a brief line per folder saying what changed there. Show non-test folders only, and ignore README files and comment-only changes.
- **Keep working through a multi-step plan without pausing for approval of each step** — aggregate the steps into one substantial change to review, and stop only for an action that reaches the world (a release, a fleet-wide effect, anything irreversible) or a decision only the owner can make.
- **Never schedule a self check-in to poll a PR** — no recurring wake-up, routine, or `send_later` re-arm that re-reads a PR's state, CI or mergeability on a timer. Act on PR events when they arrive; when nothing has arrived, end the turn.

content.text:
You're right, and the evidence is fairly clean. Here's what I found.

**What the skill actually is now.** After yesterday's change its entire body is two paragraphs, each of which says "for this kind of repo, the standard applies — see that pack's skill." It is a routing table with two hard-coded destinations and no content of its own.

**Three concrete costs:**

1. **Its links dangle in most members.** `computeVendorSet` builds the vendor set from the *declared* entries ([`vendoring/compute-vendor-set.mjs:151`](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/blob/main/vendoring/compute-vendor-set.mjs#L151)), so a repo declaring `basics` but not `static-website` never receives `packs/static-website/`. Both of the skill's links point there. `basics` is declared by every member; `chrome-extension` and `static-website` are declared by a handful — so in most repos this skill's only content is two links to files that aren't in the mount. No check catches it: `pack-independence` bars cross-pack *imports*, not doc links, and the `barriers` rules configured here guard `engine → packs/*`, not `packs/basics → packs/*`.

2. **It goes stale on someone else's schedule.** I had to rewrite it in [#1151](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/1151) purely because those two packs changed their bump story. That's the coupling billing itself.

3. **It isn't even the general answer.** [`app-store-release`](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/tree/main/packs/app-store-release) and [`play-store-release`](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/tree/main/packs/play-store-release) contain no versioning content at all — I grepped both for "version" and got zero hits. So the router covers exactly the two packs that already own their bump story completely, and says nothing for the other release packs. A repo on those gets nothing from it either way.

**The one real thing it buys**, and it's movable: your trigger phrase. `"bump version"` appears verbatim in the skill index only here, so typing it reliably loads *something*. Neither destination skill's description carries the phrase — they say "versioning" and "date-anchored version scheme". Adding the literal phrase to those two descriptions routes it to the pack that owns the answer, and only in repos that declare that pack — strictly better than a router that fires everywhere and knows two answers.

The residual after deletion is a repo declaring neither pack typing "bump version". The honest answer there is "this project has no version scheme — which files carry the version?", which needs no skill to produce.

So: I'd delete it and move the phrase. The one thing I'd flag as genuinely uncovered either way is that the two store-release packs have no version story at all — the basics skill was never filling that, but it may have been masking that nobody noticed.

input.body:
Closes #1150.

## The problem

Both release standards wrote the version themselves — the extension's daily run patch-bumped and
pushed to `main` before packaging, the site's publish reusable computed `<major>.<ymmdd>.<n>` and
pushed it before tagging. So the version a reviewer saw on a PR was never the version that shipped,
and the one push a pipeline made to `main` unattended was the one that could fail non-fast-forward
and strand a release. Claudinite holds the opposite line on itself — `pack-version-bumped`,
`engine-release-record`. These two packs now hold it too.

## What lands

**A work-scope check per pack**, gated on the repo shipping the pipeline and scoped by the repo's
own declaration of what ships:

| check | fires when |
|---|---|
| `cer/version-bumped` | the change touches something under `ship_paths` and the manifest version did not rise |
| `sw/version-bumped` | the change touches the publish set and `version_files` did not rise |

Both are silent on a change that ships nothing (a README, a test, a workflow), and both defer to the
neighbouring check (`cer/version-sync`, `sw/version-scheme`) on an off-scheme version rather than
reporting it twice.

**The pipelines stop writing versions.** Each now asks the release list whether the version on `main`
has been released yet, rather than diffing files against a tag — idempotent by construction, so a
failed run retries with nothing to undo and a push carrying an already-released version is a clean
no-op. The extension's `create-package` already worked this way; the daily run just loses its `bump`
job.

**The deliberate bump stays, as a dispatch**, because it belongs to no single change: `mode: bump`
with `part: minor|major` on the extension orchestrator, `bump: major` on the site's (the
date-anchored scheme has no minor). Each calls a new vendored reusable that raises the version,
pushes it, and lets the ordinary release path ship it.

**`basics`' `bump-version` skill is retired** (last commit). Once the routine bump belongs to the
change, that skill's whole body was a two-entry routing table into `chrome-extension` and
`static-website` — and it earned none of its place:

- its links **dangled for most members**: `computeVendorSet` builds the vendor set from the
  *declared* entries, so a repo declaring `basics` without `static-website` never receives
  `packs/static-website/`, and `basics` is declared everywhere while those two are declared by a
  handful. Nothing caught it — `pack-independence` bars cross-pack *imports*, not doc links;
- it went **stale on another pack's schedule** — the file was rewritten one commit earlier for no
  reason but that those two packs changed;
- it was **never the general answer**: `app-store-release` and `play-store-release` carry no
  versioning content at all, so the router covered exactly the two packs that already owned their
  bump story end to end.

What it genuinely bought was the trigger phrase — `"bump version"` appeared verbatim in the skill
index only there. That moves into the description of each skill that owns an answer, where it routes
to the pack that has one, and only in a repo that declares it.

Owner decisions taken in the session: the extension's daily job stays and releases when the version
on `main` has not been released yet; the site keeps `<major>.<ymmdd>.<n>`, so a PR-time bump anchors
the date to when the change was authored.

## Folders touched

```
packs/chrome-extension/
  cer/version-bumped (new work rule) + its tests; the daily reusable loses its bump job and
  asks the release list instead; a new chrome-extension-bump-version.yml reusable; the
  orchestrator gains mode: bump / part; bump.mjs gains minor/major/--print/compare and becomes
  importable; read-release-config exports a pure parse for the check to share; pack version,
  vendored-file lists, migration materialize list, README catalog row, and the release standard
  (which now carries the "bump version" trigger phrase in its description).

packs/static-website/
  sw/version-bumped (new work rule) + its tests; the publish reusable loses its bump job and
  asks the release list instead; a new static-site-bump-version.yml reusable; the orchestrator
  gains bump: major; bump.mjs gains --major/--print/compare; pack version, vendored-file lists,
  migration materialize list, RULES.md version rule, README catalog rows, and the release standard
  (which now carries the trigger phrase too).
  Separately: the standing vendoring record now materializes export-build-vars.mjs, which it had
  been omitting — a repo declaring build_vars could not self-heal onto a copy that honours it.

packs/basics/
  the bump-version skill is deleted and dropped from the pack's skills list.

engine-tests/
  the chrome vendoring round-trip counts one more workflow.
```

## Verification

- `node --test $(git ls-files '*.test.mjs')` — 2422 tests, 0 failures.
- `check_the_world` — 0 blocking, 71 advisory, byte-identical to `main`'s output.
- `check_the_work --changed` — clean.
- Both new checks were written failing-case first; their tests assert the finding's file, severity
  and wording on the miss, and silence on each of the deliberately-free cases.

## Not covered

- `app-store-release` and `play-store-release` carry no versioning or bump content at all. The
  retired basics skill was not covering that gap either, but it may have been masking it.
- The canon's own dead `.github/actions/bump-extension-patch/` and `.github/workflows/chrome-extension-*`
  copies — the pre-vendoring core plumbing the vendoring migration's header says stays until someone
  sweeps it by hand — are left as they are and now differ from the pack's stubs. Nothing executes them.

import re

def strip(path):
    lines = open(path).read().split('\n')
    out, i, removed = [], 0, 0
    while i < len(lines):
        # A version-history comment: a `// <version>: …` line plus its wrapped
        # continuations, sitting immediately above `version:`.
        if re.match(r'^\s*// (?:\d{5,6}\.\d+|\d+): ', lines[i]):
            i += 1
            removed += 1
            while i < len(lines) and re.match(r'^\s*// ', lines[i]) and not re.match(r'^\s*// (?:\d{5,6}\.\d+|\d+): ', lines[i]):
                # stop if this comment introduces the NEXT declaration rather than
                # continuing the history entry
                nxt = lines[i]
                if re.match(r'^\s*version:', lines[i + 1] if i + 1 < len(lines) else ''):
                    # a trailing comment that belongs to `version:` itself, not history
                    break
                i += 1
                removed += 1
            continue
        out.append(lines[i])
        i += 1
    open(path, 'w').write('\n'.join(out))

attachment.content:
- bump-version: Raise the project's version — a minor bump by default. Use when the owner says "bump version".
- do-later: File a change to be made AFTER the work in flight — a well-defined issue, marked for the queue and blocked behind the current PR/issue and behind the previous deferral, so repeated asks chain. Use when the owner says "/do-later …", "do this after this lands", or otherwise defers a change instead of derailing the session.
- verify-in-production: Decide whether a change that has merged can only be proven in production, and if so file the verification that comes back on its own once it is live. Use immediately after the merge, beside the conversation capture — never before, and not on request.

content.content:
---
name: merge-to-main
description: Merge the change in front of the owner into main. Use when the owner says "LGTM" or asks to merge/land the current branch or PR into main.
---

# Merge to main

If the project's own `CLAUDE.md` names a merge-policy file, that file overrides the divergent
points below (merge method, CI gating). Don't go hunting for one it doesn't name.

1. Load `create_pull_request` + `merge_pull_request` in one `ToolSearch`.
2. No PR open for the branch? `create_pull_request` (base `main`), body ending `Closes #<issue>`.
3. If the PR has check runs, wait for them to pass. None — merge without waiting.
4. `merge_pull_request`, `merge_method: squash`, title `<subject> (#<pr>)`. Don't pre-read
   mergeability; the call fails loudly.
5. Sync local `main`: `git checkout main && git pull origin main`.
6. Capture the conversation:
   `node .claudinite/shared/packs/claudinite-growth/capture-log.mjs --issue <n>`
   (in the canon repo: `node packs/claudinite-growth/capture-log.mjs --issue <n>`). Skip only if
   the repo doesn't declare `claudinite-growth`. A later merge in the same session runs it again.
7. Run the basics pack's
   [verify-in-production](../../../basics/skills/verify-in-production/SKILL.md) skill, unasked.
   This step is that skill's **only** trigger — it files against what the squash actually landed,
   which is why it runs here and not when the code was written or the PR opened. It decides
   whether this change needs a production check at all — most don't — and files the issue that
   comes back once the change is live. Never offer the owner to check later instead.

Don't re-read the issue to confirm it closed — `Closes #<issue>` does that on merge.

# The CANON repo's own CI — Claudinite's test suite + its own conformance sweep
# on every PR. Not consumer wiring (consumers ship no workflow, #385).
name: CI
on:
  pull_request:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  # Dispatchable so a GITHUB_TOKEN-authored PR (whose push/open GitHub never
  # turns into a pull_request run — the recursion guard) can still get this
  # suite started on its branch: baselining's deliver() and any bot-authored
  # PR flow (#432, #565) dispatch it explicitly.
  workflow_dispatch:
defaults:
  run:
    shell: bash
jobs:
  test-and-conformance:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
        with:
          fetch-depth: 0
          # Check out the PR's real head, not the synthetic refs/pull/N/merge commit
          # actions/checkout uses by default — otherwise HEAD is an ephemeral merge of
          # the branch into main, which the work-scoped squash-merge-history check would
          # (correctly, for that synthetic commit) flag. This makes CI evaluate exactly
          # what the local Stop hook does: the branch tip. Falls back to github.sha on push.
          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha || github.sha }}
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20
      - name: Unit tests
        # THE test roots — a closed set of FOLDERS, each swept to any depth. Depth is
        # deliberately not enumerated: the previous form spelled out one glob per level of
        # nesting, so a test at an unlisted depth was silently never run — which is exactly
        # how vendoring/'s two files sat outside CI. `**` removes depth from the question;
        # what remains is the root list, and engine-tests/ci-test-roots.test.mjs fails the
        # moment a tracked test lands outside it. Adding a root is a deliberate CI edit;
        # adding a test is not.
        #   engine-tests/            engine/ (migrations included) + the other top-level canon code;
        #                            mirrors engine/'s inner structure, and stays canon-side
        #                            because engine/ ships to consumers exactly as-is (#385)
        #   packs/                   every canon pack's tests, each inside the pack it covers
        #   vendoring/               co-located with the vendor computer/writer they cover,
        #                            the fixture-consumer rehearsal included
        #   dev/tools/               maintainer-side tooling nothing at session time runs
        #   .claudinite/local/packs/ this repo's own local packs — tests live inside the tree
        #   docs/tasks-dispatch/sim/ the dispatch design's executable scenarios — the
        #                            simulator lives beside the spec it models, not in
        #                            engine/ (nothing ships it; it tests prose)
        # nullglob: a root with no tests drops out instead of reaching node as a literal pattern.
        run: |
          shopt -s globstar nullglob

# The CANON repo's own CI — Claudinite's test suite + its own conformance sweep
# on every PR. Not consumer wiring (consumers ship no workflow, #385).
name: CI
on:
  pull_request:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  # Dispatchable so a GITHUB_TOKEN-authored PR (whose push/open GitHub never
  # turns into a pull_request run — the recursion guard) can still get this
  # suite started on its branch: baselining's deliver() and any bot-authored
  # PR flow (#432, #565) dispatch it explicitly.

defaults:
  run:
    shell: bash
jobs:
  test-and-conformance:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest

          fetch-depth: 0

          # the branch into main, which the work-scoped squash-merge-history check would
          # (correctly, for that synthetic commit) flag. This makes CI evaluate exactly
          # what the local Stop hook does: the branch tip. Falls back to github.sha on push.
          ref: ${{ github.event.pull_request.head.sha || github.sha }}
      - uses: actions/setup-node@v4
        with:
          node-version: 20
      - name: Unit tests

        # deliberately not enumerated: the previous form spelled out one glob per level of
        # nesting, so a test at an unlisted depth was silently never run — which is exactly
        # how vendoring/'s two files sat outside CI. `**` removes depth from the question;
        # what remains is the root list, and engine-tests/ci-test-roots.test.mjs fails the
        # moment a tracked test lands outside it. Adding a root is a deliberate CI edit;
        # adding a test is not.
        #   engine-tests/            engine/ (migrations included) + the other top-level canon code;
        #                            mirrors engine/'s inner structure, and stays canon-side
        #                            because engine/ ships to consumers exactly as-is (#385)
        #   packs/                   every canon pack's tests, each inside the pack it covers
        #   vendoring/               co-located with the vendor computer/writer they cover,

        #   dev/tools/               maintainer-side tooling nothing at session time runs
        #   .claudinite/local/packs/ this repo's own local packs — tests live inside the tree

        #                            engine/ (nothing ships it; it tests prose)
        # nullglob: a root with no tests drops out instead of reaching node as a literal pattern.
        run: |
          shopt -s globstar nullglob

LaughCounter's column moved today — missingbulb/LaughCounter#203 converts five, the first declarations in any member repo.

## Two members cannot carry a declaration at all

`HelloWorldFlutterApp` and `gRatio` have no `engine/checks/helpers/pattern-rules.mjs` in their mount, so their 10 rules are not a conversion backlog — they are a **convergence** finding. Both last moved 2026-08-12. Worth reading their stamps and the head sha's runs before anything else is proposed for them, per the standing "read the member's own artifacts first" rule.

## The one missing vocabulary key, with two named customers

Every content assertion in the vocabulary predicates on a file's **text**. Two fleet rules assert about a **path's existence alone**:

- `vascular-coloring/rendered-overlays-untracked` — no tracked image under `analysis/`
- `edfringe/no-stray-package-json` — no `package.json` outside the root and a grandfathered `plan/`

`repoWide.flagFilesMatching` matches text, so today these convert only by pairing a path-selecting `scanFiles` with an always-true content regex — a hack that reads as nothing. The honest form is a `forbidPathsMatching` assertion (pattern + exceptions + `what`/`fix`), which is the exact negative of the existing `requirePaths`. Both customers exist now; I'd build it against them rather than speculatively.

## What the rest of the fleet's rules actually are

All 62 were signal-classified (transcript / git / parse / derived-scan-set / config), and ~15 read in full — so treat the per-rule verdicts below as firm and the residue as classified but not individually argued to #880's standard.

The residue falls into the same classes #880 named, and the fleet is if anything *more* weighted to them, because a local pack exists precisely to carry what the canon shelf could not:

- **Derived scan set / derived key set** — the largest group. `shouts-and-whispers/cross-tier-constant-coverage` quantifies over constants discovered in one tier and looks for them in another *and* in the guard's own `PAIRS` map; `canary/pack-shape` reads the skill names out of `pack.mjs` and checks each named file exists.
- **Needs a real parser** — `edfringe-data/normalizer-selftest-in-verify` strips `step "…"` labels out of a shell script before looking for the command, precisely because a grep for the two tokens is satisfied by the label alone.
- **Computation** — `vascular-coloring/overlay-color-contrast` parses `(r, g, b)` literals and asserts `r - g >= 60 && r - b >= 60`. No pattern language expresses that, and it should not try.
- **Imports the definition it guards** — several read a constant or list out of the very code they check, which is the class where coded is the *stronger* rung.

Two near-misses worth naming, both one key from convertible:

- `on-device-privacy/on-device-speech` (LaughCounter) — asserts an opt-out appears within **12 lines after** a construction. `andIndentedBlockBelowMatches` does not fit: the opt-out sits at the same indentation, not inside a block. A "within the next N lines" relation would convert it.
- `macos-audio/swift-toolchain-gate`, `signal-teardown-routing` — both assert **ordering** (a probe sits behind a gate; `SIG_IGN` precedes `resume()`), which the vocabulary has no relation for.

## Suggested order

1. Diagnose the two stale mounts — a member that cannot compile a declaration is the blocking item, and it is not about checks at all.
2. `forbidPathsMatching`, red-first against its two customers, then convert them in their repos.
3. Judge the "within the next N lines" relation on its own merits, with `on-device-speech` as the single customer — one customer may not earn a key, and #880's `matchAnyValueOfSet` is the precedent for declining.

LaughCounter's column moved today — missingbulb/LaughCounter#203 converts five, the first declarations in any member repo.

## Two members cannot carry a declaration at all

`HelloWorldFlutterApp` and `gRatio` have no `engine/checks/helpers/pattern-rules.mjs` in their mount, so their 10 rules are not a conversion backlog — they are a **convergence** finding. Both last moved 2026-08-12. Worth reading their stamps and the head sha's runs before anything else is proposed for them, per the standing "read the member's own artifacts first" rule.

## The one missing vocabulary key, with two named customers

Every content assertion in the vocabulary predicates on a file's **text**. Two fleet rules assert about a **path's existence alone**:

- `vascular-coloring/rendered-overlays-untracked` — no tracked image under `analysis/`
- `edfringe/no-stray-package-json` — no `package.json` outside the root and a grandfathered `plan/`

`repoWide.flagFilesMatching` matches text, so today these convert only by pairing a path-selecting `scanFiles` with an always-true content regex — a hack that reads as nothing. The honest form is a `forbidPathsMatching` assertion (pattern + exceptions + `what`/`fix`), which is the exact negative of the existing `requirePaths`. Both customers exist now; I'd build it against them rather than speculatively.

## What the rest of the fleet's rules actually are

All 62 were signal-classified (transcript / git / parse / derived-scan-set / config), and ~15 read in full — so treat the per-rule verdicts below as firm and the residue as classified but not individually argued to #880's standard.

The residue falls into the same classes #880 named, and the fleet is if anything *more* weighted to them, because a local pack exists precisely to carry what the canon shelf could not:

- **Derived scan set / derived key set** — the largest group. `shouts-and-whispers/cross-tier-constant-coverage` quantifies over constants discovered in one tier and looks for them in another *and* in the guard's own `PAIRS` map; `canary/pack-shape` reads the skill names out of `pack.mjs` and checks each named file exists.
- **Needs a real parser** — `edfringe-data/normalizer-selftest-in-verify` strips `step "…"` labels out of a shell script before looking for the command, precisely because a grep for the two tokens is satisfied by the label alone.
- **Computation** — `vascular-coloring/overlay-color-contrast` parses `(r, g, b)` literals and asserts `r - g >= 60 && r - b >= 60`. No pattern language expresses that, and it should not try.
- **Imports the definition it guards** — several read a constant or list out of the very code they check, which is the class where coded is the *stronger* rung.

Two near-misses worth naming, both one key from convertible:

- `on-device-privacy/on-device-speech` (LaughCounter) — asserts an opt-out appears within **12 lines after** a construction. `andIndentedBlockBelowMatches` does not fit: the opt-out sits at the same indentation, not inside a block. A "within the next N lines" relation would convert it.
- `macos-audio/swift-toolchain-gate`, `signal-teardown-routing` — both assert **ordering** (a probe sits behind a gate; `SIG_IGN` precedes `resume()`), which the vocabulary has no relation for.

## Suggested order

1. Diagnose the two stale mounts — a member that cannot compile a declaration is the blocking item, and it is not about checks at all.
2. `forbidPathsMatching`, red-first against its two customers, then convert them in their repos.
3. Judge the "within the next N lines" relation on its own merits, with `on-device-speech` as the single customer — one customer may not earn a key, and #880's `matchAnyValueOfSet` is the precedent for declining.

Still running. While it finishes — the diagnosis so far, stated at the confidence I actually have:

**What failed:** `packs/claudinite-fleet-sheepdog/tasks/fleet-add-missing-packs/canon-packs.test.mjs:43`, test `loadCanonPacks: returns the WHOLE canon corpus, not the caller's mount`. `failureType: 'hookFailed'` — the assertions passed; the **teardown** threw `ENOTEMPTY: directory not empty, rmdir '/tmp/fit-canon-src-…/acme/Claudinite.git/.git'`.

**Why it isn't this PR's:** my diff touches nothing in `claudinite-fleet-sheepdog`; the test predates my branch (landed in #1081); `main` at my exact base is green; and the suite passes locally 3× including at CI's oversubscribed concurrency (8 workers on 4 cores).

**What I checked and ruled out**, rather than assuming:
- *Hook ordering.* The fixture registers `t.after(canon.cleanup)` before `t.after(dispose)`, and node runs `after` hooks in registration order — so the source is deleted before the clone is disposed. But `dispose` removes a different tree (`claudinite-canon-*`, the clone), not the one that threw. Not it.
- *Background auto-gc.* The fixture `git commit`s a copy of the whole corpus, which would trip `gc.auto` and leave a detached process writing into `.git` during teardown. I measured it: 754 loose objects against a 6700 threshold. Not it either.

So I do **not** have a root cause, and I'm not going to dress the retry-budget hardening (`rmSync` recursive defaults to `maxRetries: 0`) up as one — that's a mitigation for a race I haven't identified. What I can say firmly is that it's a teardown-only failure under CI's I/O contention, in code this PR doesn't touch.

The repo's rules allow exactly one re-run to confirm a failure that isn't the PR's, which is what's in flight. If it comes back red a second time, that's a real failure and I'll treat it as one rather than merging.

> ⚠️ Still open: [#1151](https://github.com/missingbulb/Claudinite/pull/1151) is unmerged — CI re-run in progress after a teardown failure in `canon-packs.test.mjs` that I've established is not this PR's but have **not** root-caused. I'll merge only if the re-run is green, and file the flake as its own issue (none exists — I searched) stating the two hypotheses I disproved rather than a guess. Also still unswept: the changelog-comment pattern in seven other packs, and the store-release packs' missing version story.
